SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WEATHER ITS RESOURCES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Weather its resources helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: WEATHER ITS RESOURCES
Weather its resources is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Explain what Weather its resources means using everyday Kenyan examples

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Weather its resources means using everyday Kenyan examples. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Weather its resources means using everyday Kenyan examples.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Weather its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Weather its resources means using everyday Kenyan examples. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how Weather its resources appears at home, school, or in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how Weather its resources appears at home, school, or in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how Weather its resources appears at home, school, or in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Weather its resources matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how Weather its resources appears at home, school, or in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise one safe skill connected to Weather its resources

What this means
In this part you learn to practise one safe skill connected to Weather its resources. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise one safe skill connected to Weather its resources.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Weather its resources this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise one safe skill connected to Weather its resources. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Tell why Weather its resources matters for life in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to tell why Weather its resources matters for life in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: tell why Weather its resources matters for life in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Weather its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can tell why Weather its resources matters for life in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Weather its resources is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Weather its resources” around your school. (skill: explain what Weather its resources means using everyday Kenyan examples)

Example 2: Say why Weather its resources matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe how Weather its resources appears at home, school, or in the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Weather its resources this week. (skill: practise one safe skill connected to Weather its resources)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Weather its resources” around your school. (skill: tell why Weather its resources matters for life in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Weather its resources to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Weather its resources means using everyday Kenyan examples.
3. Practise this skill: describe how Weather its resources appears at home, school, or in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: practise one safe skill connected to Weather its resources.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Weather its resources from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Weather its resources: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Weather its resources?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Weather its resources means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Weather its resources means using everyday Kenyan examples.
5. Be able to: describe how Weather its resources appears at home, school, or in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
